_note: Deepest wiring pass yet on Indonesia's unlinked-node backlog (105/118 unlinked as of this round's start). Two channels produced nearly all edges: BPS national compendia whose own abstracts list exact component surveys, and Bank Indonesia/OJK standards-adoption pages. Domestic BPS-to-BPS arithmetic chains (as expected from the candidates-tier precedent) were almost never stated explicitly. All quotes spot-checked and confirmed verbatim by the orchestrating session before minting.

reports.title: Framework for the Development of Environment Statistics (FDES 2013)
reports.description: UNSD's conceptual and statistical framework (2013) for organizing environment statistics across seven components (environmental conditions/quality, resources, residuals, extreme events, human settlements/environmental health, environment protection/resource management, socio-economic and cross-cutting topics). Adopted by BPS Indonesia since 2015 as the organizing framework for its annual environmental statistics compendium.
reports.cadence_note: A conceptual statistics framework, revised on a multi-decade/irregular cycle, not a periodic release.

dependencies.basis: BPS's General Government Accounts publication states its accounting framework switched to SNA 2008 in 2016: "Since 2016, the Publication of General Government Accounts has referred to the System of National Accounts (SNA) 2008 as the United Nations Statistics Division (UNSD) recommendation."

The monthly Manufacturing Production Index publication states it is compiled "using the 2010 Base Year = 100, and based on the Klasifikasi Baku Lapangan Usaha Indonesia (KBLI) 2-digits 2020. The KBLI presented in this publication is based on the 'International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities (ISIC)' Revision 4 of 2015."

The 2025 Welfare Indicators publication abstract lists every component source explicitly: "The data used is sourced from BPS and several ministries/agencies related to the presented themes. BPS data comes from the National Socioeconomic Survey (Susenas), the National Labor Force Survey (Sakernas), the Village Potential Census (Podes), the 2020 Population Census, and the Population Projections of Indonesia 2020-2050."
Same Welfare Indicators abstract as the Susenas edge above, naming the National Labor Force Survey (Sakernas) as a component source.
Same Welfare Indicators abstract as the Susenas edge above, naming the Village Potential Census (Podes) as a component source.
Same Welfare Indicators abstract as the Susenas edge above, naming the 2020 Population Census as a component source.
Same Welfare Indicators abstract as the Susenas edge above, naming the Population Projections of Indonesia 2020-2050 as a component source.

Statistik Pendidikan 2025: "The data presented includes several main indicators of educational processes and achievements based on the results of the National Socio-Economic Survey conducted in March 2025."

Statistik Kriminal 2024-2025: "The approach used in this publication covers three main aspects: crime incidents (Police administrative records), crime victims (National Socioeconomic Survey data), and regional aspects (Village Potential Data)."
Same Statistik Kriminal 2024-2025 quote as the Susenas edge above, naming Village Potential Data (Podes) as the source of the regional-aspects component.
Victimisation statistics are the Susenas-sourced component of Statistik Kriminal, per the same source-breakdown quoted for id-crime-stats above ("crime victims (National Socioeconomic Survey data)").
Profil Statistik Kesehatan 2023 is described as "sourced from data from the March 2023 National Socio-Economic Survey (Susenas)."

Bank Indonesia's SDDS metadata hub states "the data shown in this page correspond to the data described on the International Monetary Fund's Dissemination Standards Bulletin Board (DSBB)" and lists "International Reserves and Foreign Currency Liquidity" by name among Indonesia's SDDS data categories.
Same Bank Indonesia SDDS metadata hub, listing "Total Gross External Debt" by name among Indonesia's SDDS External Sector data categories.
Same Bank Indonesia SDDS metadata hub, listing "Analytical Accounts of the Banking Sector" (monetary aggregates including M1, M2) by name among Indonesia's SDDS Financial Sector data categories.

BPS's own presentation on the 2020 Population Census, delivered to the UN Statistical Commission's COVID-19 census expert group, lists its Legal Basis as a set of Indonesian laws plus a bulleted line item: "United Nations Recommendation 2017 / Population and Housing Census 2020." A bulleted legal-basis citation rather than a full explanatory sentence, so kept at the weakest relationship_type (cites) rather than methodology_depends_on.

OJK's own "Implementasi Kerangka Basel di Indonesia" page: "Indonesia telah mengadopsi kerangka modal Basel III" and "Kerangka permodalan untuk bank umum telah diadopsi dan diatur terutama melalui POJK No. 11/POJK.03/2016 ... sesuai dengan kerangka Basel III reform."

Statistik Lingkungan Hidup Indonesia (both the 2024 Indonesian and 2025 English editions, independently checked): "Since 2015, the presentation of environmental statistics in this publication has referred to the Framework for the Development of Environment Statistics (FDES) 2013, developed by the United Nations Statistics Division (UNSD)."

_dropped.why: The Gini/inequality indicator is almost certainly Susenas-derived (as several other BPS welfare products confirmed to be in this same round), but BPS's own concept/methodology pages for it (sirusa metadata, indicator concept pages, press releases) are JS-rendered and returned no fetchable body text stating the linkage explicitly. Worth a revisit with a real browser tool rather than WebFetch.

A third-party source states Sakernas adopted ICLS-13/ICLS-19 concepts since 2016, and one BPS press release references an "ILO standard" generically, but no BPS-primary-source sentence naming the ICLS resolution specifically was found within this round's time budget. A real lead, not confirmed.
